> A wedge desk stand for my Lume carrier board. The carrier is an 85 × 40 mm board that carries a Tuya T5AI-Core module, a 2.8" ILI9341 display, three buttons and a USB-C input. Flat on a desk the screen sits at a bad angle, so this stand lifts the display half and holds the board at a 45° viewing angle. Everything is dimensioned off the real fabricated board — the four M3 holes, the display header position, the antenna keepout.

## Design

### 2026-10-17 — Measured the board, blocked out the wedge

**1.0h**

Started Week 2 (CAD theme). Looked at the CYD desk buddy stand on MakerWorld
for the general idea — a low-profile wedge with a multi-angle display — but
that model is for a completely different board with the display already on it,
and it's under an exclusive license anyway. So this is drawn from my own board.

Pulled the real numbers out of the fabricated `lume-coaster.kicad_pcb` instead
of estimating anything:

- 85 × 40 mm outline, 1.6 mm thick
- 4× M3 holes (3.2 mm drill) at (4,4), (81,4), (4,36), (81,36)
- Display header J2 at the top-right, 9-pin 2.54 mm
- Module sockets leave the module riding ~9 mm above the carrier
- Antenna end is the right third — keeping bosses and screws clear of it

Decision: display mounts on wires (not onto the header directly) so the bezel
holds it at a free 45° angle, with a small channel for the cable. USB-C stays
panel-mounted at the rear. No battery pocket — keep the wedge thin.

Next: block out the base and bezel in Onshape.
